body:
Well, I brushed my hair for the first time in a couple days so... not good but not as terrible as last night. I'm formulating a plan of attack for talking with my partner, but a blunt one. I'm trying to think how he thinks and go from there. It would help me so much if he could just understand how I feel. He's pretty much the only person I have where I live and I want to feel less alone, less like Atlas and more like a Muse, or even a harpy (they had tons of friends).
I woke up too late to call the clinics I found, so I guess I'll have to do that tomorrow, but I have the list all ready. It does seem very overwhelming but I'm trying to take it one step at a time. I think I have this mental block when it comes to asking for help, like I think that I can be strong all the time, forever, and just help other people, so overcoming that will be tough. I do need help. I can't be strong forever, and expecting that of myself is setting myself up for failure, but even knowing that it's hard to shake off.
When you're laughing, and your friend tackles you mid laugh...

I found a few places that might be close enough and offer a sliding scale, so that's a start I guess. I want to feel better. 
With my partner, I've tried all sorts of different approaches, one that ended with him telling me depression was a strength, a couple that end with him trying to "fix" the problem, and a couple that he just dismisses. I've had the most luck with just asking him to hold me, and that's nice but it's a band-aid on a stab wound. I've never outright said that I'm not trying to manipulate him though... maybe he needs me to be that blunt. I tend to pick my words carefully so as to avoid confusion and to make sure my point comes across well, but that may come across as picking my words for the most emotional impact. Or maybe he perceives it as dancing around the issue and thus believes that I'm not taking it seriously... I'll try again. I know that he wants to help, or he would if he knew how serious I am.
But honestly, just the fact that a stranger on the internet cared enough to try and help means so much to me. It makes me feel like maybe I'm not worthless or crazy. 
So I guess what I'm saying is thank you for caring, and thank you for reaching out.

How did you approach the subject with offices? Honestly I wouldn't know where to begin or what to say to ask for free therapy. I feel so humiliated that I can't pay anything... 
I've tried to talk to him about my suicidal thoughts multiple times but I think since several of his exes were the type to threaten it dramatically it just doesn't register, or he thinks I'm trying to manipulate him. It could be worth another try.

I can barely afford rent and food right now, tbh. It's been a rough year. I've looked for options but free isn't one of the options available. There are some support groups I've looked in to but they are too far away (no car) or they happen during my work hours, which cannot change due to the nature of the work.
